This allows the rasterizer to terminate early-depth testing for a primitive if at least one fragment shader instance was invoked (i.e., one fragment is visible) [S3][S4, unofficial].

The claim states that the representative fragment test allows the rasterizer to terminate early-depth testing for a primitive if at least one fragment shader instance was invoked. Source [S3] explicitly defines the 'Representative Fragment Test' extension with the exact wording: 'An extension that allows the rasterizer to terminate early-depth testing earlier if at least one fragment shader instance was invoked.' Source [S4] corroborates this by stating that the method leverages the 'representative fragment test [KTB*18] extension, which allows the rasterizer to terminate early-depth testing even earlier for every primitive, if at least one fragment shader instance was invoked, that is, when one fragment of the primitive is visible.' Both sources confirm the mechanism described in the claim.
